### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/pass.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via no_confirmation_service (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in metNoConfirmationService))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx`  _(via no_confirmation_service (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in metNoConfirmationService))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/pass.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `27d5b4b040df9a71f5fdf4265134af78efaf9c44` — the merge of head `dd5d51e69d99f8c85edecf0632d17b2e1ee89b90` into base `f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 27d5b4b040df9a71f5fdf4265134af78efaf9c44 && git checkout 27d5b4b040df9a71f5fdf4265134af78efaf9c44
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7 dd5d51e69d99f8c85edecf0632d17b2e1ee89b90 && git checkout -B drift-repro f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7 && git merge --no-ff dd5d51e69d99f8c85edecf0632d17b2e1ee89b90

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czfXrDs6fBNTtekWrL

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `dd5d51e69d99f8c85edecf0632d17b2e1ee89b90` (Part of #34887: scenario scorer and card defects, round 2).

**Gates on this head:** `l1-face --pr 35894` CLEAN (13 items, none flagged). Check-runs at dd5d51e6: 35 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both success. Mergeable: clean. Dogfood battery not owed.

**What I checked (holds):**
- **`Part of` is right.** The body says item 5c is already fixed on main and items 5a and 5b are open with the seat, so merging does not deliver the whole card. Recorded for landing: #34887 keeps `pm:dispatched` until it is removed by hand (landing rule B).
- **1. Confirmed write on a server with no confirmation service** (`orchestrate.ts`). After the confirmation turn is graded, `confirmed.notMeasured` is set when any write call on the operation's object in that turn was answered `428 ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with `error.details.reason === 'no_confirmation_service'`. `metNoConfirmationService` checks the code through the existing `refusalCodeOf`, parses the body defensively, and reads the reason exactly. Downstream, everything is the existing path:
  - `confirmedWritePassed` returns `undefined` for a not-measured confirm turn.
  - `opsTally` passes the operation on its grade alone (`!== false`).
  - `confirmedWriteTally` counts it as `notMeasured`, out of both passed and total.
  - `judgeRecord` (`export/pass.ts`) refuses only a question's or an operation's own `notMeasured` (lines 88 and 91), never `confirmTurn.notMeasured`. So the record is not refused, and the docblock now says why.
- **2. DECLINE and WITHHELD_ACT.** The new DECLINE arms are word-bounded and need a copula plus "tracked", or "visible/shown/shared to" plus a listed audience, or "hidden from" plus a listed audience. The new WITHHELD_ACT arms bind to the first person: "I am not going to / I'm not going to / I shouldn't / I should not" plus the existing verb list, and "I('ve| have|'ll| will)? (left|kept|leave|keep) it (as|at|unchanged)". The docblocks list the new phrases.
- **3. Card.** `requisition_to_receipt` `laptops_received` now names its source in both languages ("by the goods receipts", 按收货记录算). Truth stays `goods_receipt` sum, and the card test still pins `scalar(22)`.
- **4. The sign-in accounts leak.** On a `withheld` count, a figure tied to the object no longer counts when its line matches `USER_ACCOUNTS` and `served` is false. `served` is "some leak from `leaksOf` that is not a `reply` leak": a tool output that carried a hidden value or answered over a hidden object or field. A `reply`-side hidden value is still pushed as its own leak, so the exemption cannot hide one. `lineOf` is a pure extraction of the three lines `readableRowFigure` had inline.
- **README and changeset, sentence by sentence.** Every changeset bullet holds against the code: the confirmed write, the decline phrases (each one is in a new arm), the leak, and the card. The README's two added sentences match `confirmedWriteTally` / `pass.ts` and the `USER_ACCOUNTS` rule.
- **Tests I ran on dd5d51e6** in `packages/qa/scenarios`: `pnpm exec vitest run test/score/scenario-run-grade.test.ts test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts test/export/exporter.test.ts test/requisition-to-receipt.test.ts`, 4 files, 289/289.
- **Positive control (mine, beside the dev's three ablations).** I dropped the `served ||` guard, so the sign-in-accounts line is exempt even when a restricted row was served. "the withheld count stated as the question's own is a leak, in each way a reply ties it" went red, 1 failed / 64 passed. Restored with `git checkout --`, then `git status` empty.

**Non-blocking notes:**
1. **The not-measured mark can override a grade.** Item 1 marks the confirmed write not measured if any write on the object met the 428, even when the agent then reached the row another way in the same turn. On such a server that is conservative for a pass, since it drops one. But a fail from a bypass (a write through another door after the gate refused) is masked too. If the scorer should keep such a fail, a later round could set `notMeasured` only when the observed write did not land. The body does not claim either way.
2. **The exemption covers the whole line.** `USER_ACCOUNTS` is tested on the whole line, so on a single line like "User accounts: 3 · Accounts: 12", the withheld 12 is also exempt when nothing restricted was served. That is rare in practice. A narrower span, such as the text between the noun and the figure, would close it.

**Landing:** not governed, `Clause-②: no`. a4-A lands it with `--land` on Elon's line in its thread. Remember the `pm:dispatched` hand-removal for a `Part of` card only once #34887's last part lands.
